1  IN THE HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH
AT INDORE
BEFORE  HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE ANIL VERMA  ON THE 20 th OF JULY, 2023  MISC. CRIMINAL CASE No. 31427 of 2023

BETWEEN:-
 RADHESHYAM BANJARA @ BHOLA S/O SHRI KAILASH  BANJARA, AGED 19 YEARS,

OCCUPATION: LABOURER  R/O BORKHEDA VILLAGE NAGDA DISTRICT UJJAIN  (MADHYA PRADESH)
 
 (BY SHRI RAHUL MAHESHWARI - ADVOCATE)
 AND  THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH THROUGH POLICE  STATION MAHIDPUR DISTRICT UJJAIN (MADHYA  PRADESH)
 
 ( BY SMT. VARSHA SINGH THAKUR - GOVERNMENT ADVOCATE)
 This application coming on for admission this day, the   following:
 ORDER

This is the first application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of regular bail relating to Crime No. 168/2023 registered at Police Station Mahidpur District Ujjain (M.P.) for the offence under Sections 363, 343, 366-A, 376(2)(n) and 376D A of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and section 3,4(2), 5l, 5g and 6 of POCSO Act.

2. As per prosecution story, on 15.4.2023 minor prosecutrix woke up in the morning and went outside her house for answering the natural call at that time present applicant alongwith co-accused Sanjay came there on motorcycle and they forcibly covered her face by a cloth and threatened her that if she cries they will kill her, then they kept her in a hut where co-accused committed repeatedly rape upon her and present applicant was sitting outside the hut and keeping watch upon the persons.
After 6-7 days both the accused persons left the prosecutrix and threatened her that if she discloses the incident to her family members, they will kill her.

After sometime prosecutrix lodged Radheshyam Banjara @ Bhola vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177458618/
1 the FIR.

sentences.text: Accordingly, offence has been registered against the applicant.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is an innocent person and he has been falsely implicated in this offence.
He is in custody since 5.5.2023.
Applicant is not the main accused who has committed rape upon prosecutrix.
There is material contradiction and omission in the statement of prosecutrix.
Applicant is permanent resident of Ujjain district.
Final conclusion of the trial is likely to take sufficient long time.
Under the above circumstances, prayer for grant of bail may be considered on such terms and conditions, as this Court deems fit and proper.
4. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent / State opposes the bail application and prays for its rejection by submitting that applicant has actively participated in the incident.

5. Perused the impugned order of the trial Court as well as the case diary.
6.

After considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, nature and gravity of offence,
arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the parties it is revealed that the date of birth of prosecutrix is 24.11.2008 and at the time of incident she was aged about 14 years and four months

,
prosecutrix in her statement under section 161 Cr.P.C. categorically stated that present applicant alongwith co-accused abducted her and also threatened her for life, she was kept in a hut for a period of 6-7 days and during whole period, the applicant was present there and keeping watch on her.

In view of the active participation of applicant in the incident and the material available against the applicant, this court is not inclined to grant regular bail to applicant.
7.
Hence this first regular bail application of applicant under section 439 of Cr.P.C. is hereby dismissed.
Certified copy as per rules.

(ANIL VERMA) JUDGE BDJ Radheshyam Banjara @ Bhola vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177458618/
